the_separation: Filled completes rest a median of 1 tick(s) from the best opposite ask; unfilled ones rest a median of 2 ticks away, p75 7 and as far as 48. Distance from touch, not rest time, is what separates them: median rest 7.71s filled against 6.99s unfilled is the deadline, not a cause.
the_finding: In 176 of 475 (37.0%) unfilled completes L5's OWN touch moved above where we were sitting, and in 106 of those the opposite ask reached that new touch -- 22.3% of all unfilled completes had an L5-CONSISTENT reprice available that the book would have met. We never made it, because the touch_moved re-quote is gated to OPEN and EXTEND: 0 of 868 COMPLETEs ever exited that way, against 36 OPEN and 35 EXTEND. Placement is not the defect -- we price AT L5's touch in 74.7% of them.
upper_bound_not_an_estimate: rest_book is an AGGREGATE. min_opp_ask and max_touch are extrema over the same window and we cannot prove they coincided, so the count where both held is an UPPER BOUND on what repricing would have captured. Reaching a price is also not filling it -- we rest as maker and queue position decides -- and repricing to the touch can cross, which post-only refuses.
classification: BEHAVIORAL-FIDELITY FIX, not a new strategy: L5's touch moved and our clone did not follow it. Following L5's own price is cloning him; paying up to get filled would not be.
the_mechanism_already_exists: the live session re-quotes on touch_moved for OPEN and EXTEND and excludes COMPLETE by one condition. 36 OPEN and 35 EXTEND orders exited that way; 0 of 868 COMPLETEs did. The crossing guard (px >= opp_ask -> would_cross) already runs ahead of it for every relation. EXTEND's lower deadline share (28.5% vs 64.9%) is confounded by relation and is NOT an effect size.
